text: Stock Split: a company divides each existing share into multiple shares (e.g. 1-for-2) at a fixed ratio set by the company. Mandatory - every shareholder's position is adjusted automatically on the record date; there is no election and no deadline for the shareholder to respond to.

Bonus Issue: additional shares are credited to every shareholder pro-rata to their existing holding, funded from reserves, at no cost. Mandatory - applied automatically to all eligible holders on the record date, no election required.

Cash Dividend: a fixed cash amount per share is paid to all shareholders of record. Mandatory - the amount and eligibility are fixed by the company; the shareholder has no choice in whether or how much to receive.
Stock Dividend: additional shares (rather than cash) are distributed to shareholders based on a fixed ratio. Mandatory - applied automatically like a bonus issue, no shareholder election involved.

Reverse Stock Split (Consolidation): multiple existing shares are combined into one at a fixed ratio (e.g. 5-for-1), typically to raise the per-share price. Mandatory - applied to all holders automatically on the record date.

Spin-off: a company distributes shares of a subsidiary or division to existing shareholders as a new, separately listed entity. Usually mandatory - shares are distributed automatically pro-rata; the shareholder does not choose whether to receive them (though they may later choose to sell).

Straight Merger: shareholders of the acquired company automatically receive a fixed number of acquirer shares per share held, with no choice of consideration type. Mandatory - the exchange ratio is fixed, no election window.

Ticker or Company Name Change: an administrative corporate action updating the security's identifier or the issuer's registered name, with no change to the underlying holding. Mandatory - purely a reference-data update, no shareholder action possible or required.

Involuntary Delisting: a security is removed from an exchange by regulatory or exchange action rather than shareholder choice. Mandatory in the sense that shareholders have no election - though it may trigger a downstream requirement to transfer to an off-market/OTC record, that transfer itself is procedural, not elective.

Coupon or Interest Payment (on a bond or convertible instrument): a scheduled fixed payment made automatically to the holder of record. Mandatory - amount and timing are contractually fixed, no shareholder election.

Rights Issue: existing shareholders are offered the right to buy additional shares at a discounted price, in proportion to their holding, within a defined subscription window. Voluntary - the shareholder must actively elect to subscribe, sell the rights, or let them lapse; missing the deadline forfeits the entitlement.

Voluntary Tender Offer (Buyback): the company or an acquirer offers to purchase shares from willing holders at a stated price within a tender window. Voluntary - each shareholder decides independently whether to tender some, all, or none of their holding by the deadline.

Convertible Bond Conversion: the bondholder has the contractual option to convert the bond into a fixed number of equity shares, usually within a conversion window or up to maturity. Voluntary - the holder must actively instruct conversion; absent an instruction the bond remains a bond.

Merger with Election: shareholders of the acquired company may choose between cash, acquirer stock, or a mix, within an election deadline, subject to proration. Voluntary - a default consideration usually applies only if no election is submitted, and that default should be confirmed rather than assumed.

Dividend Reinvestment Plan (DRIP): a shareholder may opt to have cash dividends automatically reinvested into additional shares instead of receiving cash. Voluntary - requires an active opt-in instruction; the default without one is a normal cash dividend.

Odd-Lot Tender Offer: a tender offer specifically for holders of less than a standard trading lot, often at preferential terms to reduce small-holder administrative cost. Voluntary - eligible holders choose whether to tender within the offer window.

Warrant Exercise: the warrant holder has the right, but not the obligation, to purchase shares at a fixed strike price before expiry. Voluntary - requires an active exercise instruction and payment of the strike price by the expiry deadline, otherwise the warrant lapses worthless.

Consent Solicitation: an issuer asks bondholders to vote on proposed changes to bond covenants or terms, sometimes with a consent fee for responding by the deadline. Voluntary - requires the holder to actively submit a vote/consent; non-response is itself a choice with consequences for eligibility of any fee.
